Johnson's basis is further reduced by the property's carryover basis ($12,000) but is limited to Johnson's $9,000 remaining basis. Therefore, Johnson's basis in the property is $9,000.
questions.explanationJa: 当期の通常所得の持分50%×$6,000＝$3,000でベーシスは$14,000＋$3,000＝$17,000に増え、そこから現金の分配$8,000を引いて$9,000が残る。資産の引継ぎ帳簿価額$12,000は残りのベーシス$9,000に制限されるので、分配された資産のベーシスは$9,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.57

questions.stem:
Brooke and Bulstrode are equal partners in the B&B Partnership, a cash basis tax entity with the following balance sheet items:

Adjusted tax basis | Fair market value
Cash | $250 | $250
Accounts receivable | 0 | 300
Total assets | $250 | $550
Accounts payable | $150 | $150
Brooke, capital | 50 | 200
Bulstrode, capital | 50 | 200
Total liabilities and capital | $250 | $550

On the balance sheet date, Brooke purchases Bulstrode's 50% interest in the partnership, paying Bulstrode $300 cash and assuming Bulstrode's share of the partnership liabilities. As a result of this buyout of her partnership interest, what is the capital gain on sale that Bulstrode should report on her individual tax return?
questions.explanation:
Generally, the sale of a P/S interest is a capital gain (loss) because it results from the sale of a capital asset. At the time of sale, if the P/S has unrealized ordinary income assets, referred to as hot assets (unrealized receivables, appreciated inventory), the partner has effectively converted ordinary income to capital gains. To prevent this, the capital gain is recharacterized as ordinary income to the extent of the partner's share of hot assets at the time of sale.

In this scenario, Bulstrode realized a gain of $250, as calculated below. Because the P/S has a hot asset (unrealized accounts receivable [A/R]), $150 of the gain is recharacterized as ordinary. Accordingly, Bulstrode reports a capital gain of $100 ($250 − $150).

Cash received: $300
Relief of liabilities ($150 × 50%): 75
Amount realized: $375
Less adjusted outside basis ($50 capital + $75 liabilities): (125)
Realized gain: $250
Recharacterized as ordinary income ($300 A/R × 50%): (150)
Reported as capital gain: $100
questions.explanationJa: 持分の売却は原則として資本資産の売却でありキャピタルゲインとなるが、パートナーシップにホットアセット（未実現債権や含み益のある棚卸資産）がある場合、その持分相当額は通常所得として扱う。Bulstrodeの実現額は、現金$300＋負債の免除$150×50%＝$75で$375である。外部ベーシスは資本$50＋負債$75＝$125なので、実現利得は$375−$125＝$250となる。現金主義の売掛金$300の50%＝$150を通常所得とするため、キャピタルゲインは$250−$150＝$100である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Partnership Taxation Q.58

questions.stem: "Hot assets" of a partnership would include which of the following?
questions.explanation:
"Hot assets" under IRC §751 are unrealized receivables and inventory items. When a partner sells a partnership interest or receives certain distributions, the portion attributable to hot assets produces ordinary income rather than capital gain. Unrealized receivables include rights to payment for goods or services not yet included in income (such as receivables of a cash-basis partnership) and depreciation recapture potential.

Cash is not a hot asset; it does not generate ordinary income on a sale of an interest.
Section 1231 assets are not hot assets, except to the extent of depreciation recapture, which is treated as an unrealized receivable.
Capital assets are not hot assets; gain attributable to them retains capital character.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §751 の「ホットアセット」とは、未実現債権（unrealized receivables）と棚卸資産（inventory items）をいう。持分の売却などの際、これらに対応する部分はキャピタルゲインではなく通常所得となる。未実現債権には、現金主義のパートナーシップの売掛金や償却の取戻し部分が含まれる。
現金はホットアセットではない。§1231 資産も（償却の取戻し部分を除き）ホットアセットではない。資本資産もホットアセットではなく、その部分の利益はキャピタルゲインのままである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2011 Recently Released Q.37 (AICPA No. 9977)

questions.stem: As a general partner in Greenland Associates, an individual's share of partnership income for the current tax year is $25,000 ordinary business income and a $10,000 guaranteed payment. The individual also received $5,000 in cash distributions from the partnership. What income should the individual report from the interest in Greenland?
questions.explanation:
A partner reports the distributive share of partnership ordinary business income and any guaranteed payments as income (IRC §§702, 707(c)). A cash distribution is not income; it reduces the partner's basis and produces gain only to the extent it exceeds the partner's basis (IRC §731(a)). Basis is first increased by the $25,000 income share before the distribution is applied, so the $5,000 distribution does not exceed basis.

Ordinary business income share = $25,000
Guaranteed payment = $10,000
Reported income = $25,000 + $10,000 = $35,000

The $5,000 amount reports only the cash distribution, which is not income.
The $25,000 amount omits the guaranteed payment, which is taxable to the partner.
The $40,000 amount adds the cash distribution, which is a nontaxable reduction of basis.
questions.explanationJa:
パートナーは、通常事業所得の分配持分とギャランティード・ペイメントを所得として申告する（IRC §702、§707(c)）。現金分配は所得ではなく持分の basis を減らすだけで、basis を超えた部分だけが利益になる（§731(a)）。分配の前に所得持分 $25,000 で basis が増えるので、$5,000 の分配は basis を超えない。
報告する所得 = $25,000 + $10,000 = $35,000。
$5,000 は分配額だけを計上している。$25,000 はギャランティード・ペイメントを漏らしている。$40,000 は非課税の分配を加えている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2011 Recently Released Q.39 (AICPA No. 9979)

questions.stem: While preparing a partnership tax return, the accountant discovered that ABC Partnership distributed property to Anne, a partner, in a nonliquidating transfer. No money was distributed to Anne during the year, the property was in the partnership for over five years, and no debt was attached to the property. Anne had a basis in her partnership interest of $10,000. The partnership had an adjusted basis of $20,000 in the property distributed to Anne. Which of the following are the tax consequences to Anne?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $0 gain, basis in the partnership is reduced to $0, and basis in the property received is $10,000

choices.label: B
choices.text: $0 gain, basis in the partnership is reduced to $0, and basis in the property received is $20,000

choices.label: C
choices.text: $10,000 gain, basis in the partnership is reduced to $0, and basis in the property received is $20,000

choices.label: D
choices.text: $10,000 gain, basis in the partnership is unchanged, and basis in the property received is $20,000

questions.explanation:
In a nonliquidating (current) distribution, a partner recognizes gain only if money distributed exceeds the partner's outside basis (IRC §731(a)(1)); no money was distributed, so no gain is recognized. The partner's basis in distributed property is the partnership's adjusted basis in the property, limited to the partner's outside basis reduced by any money received (IRC §732(a)). The outside basis is then reduced by the basis assigned to the property (IRC §733).

Gain recognized = $0
Basis in property = lesser of $20,000 partnership basis or $10,000 outside basis = $10,000
Outside basis after distribution = $10,000 - $10,000 = $0

A $20,000 basis in the property is incorrect because the property's basis cannot exceed the partner's $10,000 outside basis in a nonliquidating distribution.
Recognizing $10,000 of gain is incorrect because a distribution of property (other than money or marketable securities) does not trigger gain; the outside basis limits the property's basis instead.
Leaving the outside basis unchanged is incorrect because §733 reduces it by the basis of the property received.
questions.explanationJa:
非清算分配では、分配された金銭が持分の basis（outside basis）を超えない限り利益は認識しない（IRC §731(a)(1)）。本問は金銭の分配が無いので利益はゼロ。受け取った資産の basis はパートナーシップでの簿価だが、非清算分配では outside basis が上限となり（§732(a)）、outside basis は資産に付けた basis だけ減る（§733）。
利益 $0、資産の basis = min($20,000, $10,000) = $10,000、分配後の outside basis = $0。
資産の basis を $20,000 とするのは outside basis の上限を無視している。$10,000 の利益を認識するのは誤りで、金銭以外の資産の分配では利益は生じず basis の制限で処理する。outside basis が変わらないのも §733 に反する。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.15 (AICPA No. 89815)

questions.stem: Able and Baker are equal members in Apple, an LLC. Apple has elected not to be treated as a corporation. Able contributes $7,000 cash and Baker contributes a machine with a basis of $5,000 and a fair market value of $10,000, subject to a liability of $3,000. What is Apple's basis for the machine?
questions.explanation:
An LLC that has not elected corporate treatment and has two members is taxed as a partnership. The partnership's basis in contributed property is the contributing partner's adjusted basis at the time of contribution (IRC §723). The liability attached to the machine affects the partners' outside bases, not the partnership's inside basis in the machine.

Apple's basis in the machine = Baker's adjusted basis = $5,000

The $2,000 amount incorrectly reduces the carryover basis by the $3,000 liability.
The $8,000 amount incorrectly adds the $3,000 liability to the carryover basis.
The $10,000 amount uses fair market value, which applies only in limited situations not present here.
questions.explanationJa:
法人課税を選択していない2人以上のメンバーの LLC はパートナーシップとして課税される。拠出資産のパートナーシップでの basis は、拠出したパートナーの拠出時の簿価をそのまま引き継ぐ（IRC §723）。資産に付いた負債は各パートナーの持分の basis に影響するが、パートナーシップ内の資産の basis は変わらない。
機械の basis = $5,000。
$2,000 は負債を差し引いている。$8,000 は負債を加えている。$10,000 は時価を用いており誤り。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.24 (AICPA No. 89824)

questions.stem: In return for a 20% partnership interest, Skinner contributed $5,000 cash and land with a $12,000 basis and a $20,000 fair market value to the partnership. The land was subject to a $10,000 mortgage that the partnership assumed. In addition, the partnership had $20,000 in recourse liabilities that would be shared by partners according to their partnership interests. What amount represents Skinner's basis in the partnership interest?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §722, a partner's initial basis equals cash contributed plus the adjusted basis of contributed property. Under IRC §752, the partnership's assumption of the partner's mortgage is treated as a distribution of money to the partner (decrease), while the partner's share of partnership liabilities, including the assumed mortgage and the existing recourse liabilities, is treated as a contribution of money (increase).

Cash contributed: $5,000
Basis of land: + $12,000
Mortgage assumed by partnership: - $10,000
Share of assumed mortgage (20% x $10,000): + $2,000
Share of existing recourse liabilities (20% x $20,000): + $4,000
Basis in partnership interest = $13,000

The $27,000 amount ($5,000 + $12,000 + $10,000) adds the mortgage instead of subtracting the relief of it. The $21,000 amount ($5,000 + $12,000 + $4,000) ignores both the $10,000 mortgage relief and Skinner's $2,000 share of the assumed mortgage. The $19,000 amount ($5,000 + $20,000 - $10,000 + $4,000) uses the land's $20,000 fair market value instead of its $12,000 basis and omits the $2,000 share of the assumed mortgage.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §722により、パートナーの当初持分ベーシスは拠出現金＋拠出資産の調整後ベーシス。§752により、パートナーシップが引き受けた抵当債務は当該パートナーへの金銭分配（減算）とみなされ、引受債務・既存のリコース債務に対するパートナーの負担割合は金銭拠出（加算）とみなされる。

拠出現金 $5,000
土地のベーシス ＋$12,000
引き受けられた抵当債務 −$10,000
引受債務の自己負担分（20%×$10,000）＋$2,000
既存リコース債務の自己負担分（20%×$20,000）＋$4,000
持分ベーシス = $13,000

$27,000（$5,000＋$12,000＋$10,000）は抵当債務を減算せず加算している。$21,000（$5,000＋$12,000＋$4,000）は$10,000の債務免除と引受債務の負担分$2,000の両方を無視している。$19,000（$5,000＋$20,000−$10,000＋$4,000）は土地をベーシス$12,000ではなく時価$20,000で計上し、引受債務の負担分$2,000を落としている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2013 Recently Released Q.7 (AICPA No. 90207)

questions.stem: When the AQR partnership was formed, partner Acre contributed land with a fair market value of $100,000 and a tax basis of $60,000 in exchange for a one-third interest in the partnership. The AQR partnership agreement specifies that each partner will share equally in the partnership's profits and losses. During its first year of operation, AQR sold the land to an unrelated third party for $160,000. What is the proper tax treatment of the sale?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Each partner reports a capital gain of $33,333.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The entire gain of $100,000 must be specifically allocated to Acre.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The first $40,000 of gain is allocated to Acre, and the remaining gain of $60,000 is shared equally by the other two partners.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The first $40,000 of gain is allocated to Acre, and the remaining gain of $60,000 is shared equally by all the partners in the partnership.

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §704(c)(1), income, gain, loss, and deduction with respect to contributed property must be allocated among the partners to take into account the difference between the property's basis and its fair market value at contribution. The pre-contribution built-in gain is allocated to the contributing partner, and any post-contribution gain is shared under the partnership agreement.

Built-in gain at contribution = $100,000 FMV - $60,000 basis = $40,000 (allocated to Acre)
Total gain on sale = $160,000 - $60,000 = $100,000
Post-contribution gain = $100,000 - $40,000 = $60,000, shared equally by all three partners ($20,000 each)
Acre's total gain = $40,000 + $20,000 = $60,000

Reporting $33,333 by each partner ignores §704(c). Allocating the entire $100,000 to Acre wrongly allocates the post-contribution appreciation to Acre. Sharing the $60,000 only between the other two partners wrongly excludes Acre, who is entitled to one-third of the post-contribution gain.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §704(c)(1)により、拠出資産に係る損益は拠出時のベーシスと時価の差を考慮してパートナー間に配分しなければならない。拠出前の含み益は拠出したパートナーに配分し、拠出後の値上がり益はパートナーシップ契約に従って配分する。

拠出時の含み益 = 時価$100,000 − ベーシス$60,000 = $40,000（Acreに配分）
売却益合計 = $160,000 − $60,000 = $100,000
拠出後の利得 = $100,000 − $40,000 = $60,000 を3人で均等に（各$20,000）
Acreの利得合計 = $40,000 + $20,000 = $60,000

各パートナー$33,333は§704(c)を無視している。$100,000全額をAcreに配分するのは拠出後の値上がり益までAcreに帰属させており誤り。$60,000を他の2人だけで分けるのは、拠出後の利得の1/3を受けるべきAcreを除外しており誤り。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2013 Recently Released Q.21 (AICPA No. 90221)

questions.stem: Anderson and Decker are equal members in Andek, an LLC, which has not elected to be treated as a corporation. Anderson contributes $7,000 cash, and Decker contributes a machine with an adjusted basis of $5,000 and fair market value of $10,000, subject to a liability of $3,000. What is Decker's basis in Andek?
questions.explanation:
An LLC that has not elected corporate treatment and has two members is taxed as a partnership. Under IRC §722, a member's basis equals the adjusted basis of contributed property. Under IRC §752, the LLC's assumption of the member's liability is a deemed distribution (decrease), and the member's share of the LLC's liabilities is a deemed contribution (increase). As an equal member, Decker shares 50% of the liability.

Adjusted basis of machine: $5,000
Liability assumed by LLC: - $3,000
Decker's 50% share of liability: + $1,500
Decker's basis = $3,500

The $2,000 amount subtracts the full $3,000 liability without adding back Decker's 50% share. The $5,000 amount ignores the liability entirely. The $10,000 amount uses the machine's fair market value rather than its adjusted basis.
questions.explanationJa:
法人課税を選択していない2人のメンバーのLLCはパートナーシップとして課税される。IRC §722により、メンバーの持分ベーシスは拠出資産の調整後ベーシス。§752により、LLCによる負債引受けはみなし分配（減算）、メンバーの負債負担分はみなし拠出（加算）となる。均等メンバーのDeckerは負債の50%を負担する。

機械の調整後ベーシス $5,000
LLCが引き受けた負債 −$3,000
Deckerの負担分（50%）＋$1,500
Deckerのベーシス = $3,500

$2,000は負債$3,000を全額差し引き、自己負担分50%を加算していない。$5,000は負債を全く考慮していない。$10,000は調整後ベーシスではなく時価を使っている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2014 Recently Released Q.16 (AICPA No. 90566)

questions.stem: Able, an individual, is a partner in CD Partnership with an adjusted basis of $30,000 for Able's partnership interest. Able received a non-liquidating distribution of $25,000 cash and property with an adjusted basis of $7,000, and a fair market value of $10,000. What amount of gain should Able recognize?
questions.explanation:
In a nonliquidating (current) distribution, a partner recognizes gain only to the extent that money distributed exceeds the partner's adjusted basis in the partnership interest immediately before the distribution (IRC §731(a)(1)). Property other than money does not trigger gain.

Basis before distribution: $30,000
Cash distributed: $25,000 (less than $30,000, so no gain)
Remaining basis: $30,000 − $25,000 = $5,000
Basis of property received: lesser of the partnership's $7,000 basis or the remaining $5,000 = $5,000 (§732(a)(2))
Able's basis after the distribution: $0
Gain recognized: $0

The $2,000 amount counts the property at its $7,000 basis as if it were money ($25,000 + $7,000 − $30,000). The $5,000 amount counts the property at its $10,000 fair market value as if it were money ($25,000 + $10,000 − $30,000). The $12,000 amount counts both the $7,000 basis and the $10,000 fair market value as money ($25,000 + $7,000 + $10,000 − $30,000). Only money in excess of outside basis produces gain, and the property distributed has its basis limited to $5,000 instead.
questions.explanationJa:
現物を含む非清算分配（current distribution）では、パートナーが利得を認識するのは分配された金銭が分配直前の持分の取得価額を超える場合だけである（IRC §731(a)(1)）。金銭以外の資産の分配で利得は生じない。

分配前の持分ベーシス: $30,000
現金分配: $25,000（$30,000未満なので利得なし）
残りのベーシス: $30,000 − $25,000 = $5,000
受け取った資産の取得価額: パートナーシップ側の$7,000と残りの$5,000の小さい方 = $5,000（§732(a)(2)）
分配後のAbleの持分ベーシス: $0
認識利得: $0

$2,000は資産を取得価額$7,000の金銭として数えたもの（$25,000 + $7,000 − $30,000）、$5,000は時価$10,000の金銭として数えたもの（$25,000 + $10,000 − $30,000）、$12,000は取得価額$7,000と時価$10,000の両方を金銭として数えたもの（$25,000 + $7,000 + $10,000 − $30,000）である。利得になるのは金銭が持分ベーシスを超える部分だけで、分配された資産の取得価額は$5,000に制限されるにとどまる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2014 Recently Released Q.37 (AICPA No. 90587)

questions.stem: Kline and Salomon form the KS Partnership as 50/50 partners. Kline contributes equipment that has a fair market value of $60,000 and an adjusted basis of $45,000. In addition, the equipment is subject to a $10,000 loan that KS Partnership is assuming. What amount represents Kline's initial basis in the partnership?
questions.explanation:
A partner's initial basis equals the adjusted basis of contributed property (IRC §722), decreased by liabilities assumed by the partnership (a deemed distribution of money under §752(b)) and increased by the partner's share of partnership liabilities (a deemed contribution of money under §752(a)).

Adjusted basis of equipment: $45,000
Less liability assumed by the partnership: (10,000)
Plus Kline's 50% share of the liability: 5,000
Kline's initial basis: $40,000

The $35,000 amount subtracts the full liability without adding back Kline's 50% share. The $45,000 amount ignores the liability entirely. The $60,000 amount uses the equipment's fair market value, but contributed property carries over its adjusted basis.
questions.explanationJa:
パートナーの当初の持分ベーシスは、拠出資産の取得価額（IRC §722）から、パートナーシップが引き受けた負債（§752(b)のみなし金銭分配）を差し引き、自分のパートナーシップ負債の持分（§752(a)のみなし金銭拠出）を加えて求める。

設備の取得価額: $45,000
パートナーシップが引き受けた負債: (10,000)
Klineの負債持分50%: 5,000
Klineの当初ベーシス: $40,000

$35,000は負債全額を差し引き、自分の負担分50%を足し戻していない。$45,000は負債を無視している。$60,000は時価を使っているが、拠出資産は取得価額を引き継ぐ。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2015 Recently Released Q.15 (AICPA No. 90815)

questions.stem:
Partnership P has an operating loss of $10,000 for the year. Partner A had a 50% interest in the partnership, with a basis of $5,000 at the beginning of the year. P distributed $2,000 to A during the year.

What amount of loss is deductible by A?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §704(d), a partner's distributive share of partnership loss is deductible only to the extent of the partner's outside basis at the end of the year. In determining that limit, basis is first reduced by distributions made during the year (§733; Treas. Reg. §1.704-1(d)(2)) before losses are applied.

Beginning basis = $5,000
Less distribution = ($2,000)
Basis available for losses = $3,000
Share of loss = $10,000 × 50% = $5,000, limited to $3,000 (the remaining $2,000 is carried forward)

The $5,000 amount is the full share of loss, ignoring the reduction for the distribution. The $2,000 amount is the distribution or the suspended loss, not the deductible loss. The $7,000 amount adds the distribution to the basis instead of subtracting it.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §704(d)により、パートナーが控除できる損失の分配額は、年度末のパートナー持分の取得価額（outside basis）が上限である。上限を計算する際は、損失より先に当年の分配でbasisを減らす（§733、Treas. Reg. §1.704-1(d)(2)）。

期首basis = $5,000
分配 = ($2,000)
損失に使えるbasis = $3,000
損失の持分 = $10,000 × 50% = $5,000 → 上限$3,000（残り$2,000は繰越）

$5,000は分配によるbasisの減少を無視した額。$2,000は分配額（または繰越損失）であり控除額ではない。$7,000は分配をbasisから引かずに足している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.17 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem:
A partner received a partnership interest with a fair market value (FMV) of $55,000 in exchange for the following items:

Item | Basis | FMV
Cash | $20,000 | $20,000
Property | 10,000 | 30,000
Services rendered | 0 | 5,000

What is the partner's basis in the partnership interest?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §722, a partner's basis in an interest acquired by contributing property equals the money contributed plus the adjusted basis of contributed property. A partnership interest received for services is taxable compensation (IRC §83; Treas. Reg. §1.721-1(b)(1)), and the $5,000 included in income becomes part of the partner's basis.

Cash = $20,000
Property (adjusted basis) = $10,000
Services (amount included in income) = $5,000
Basis in partnership interest = $35,000

The $55,000 amount uses the fair market value of the interest received, and the $50,000 amount uses the property's fair market value of $30,000 instead of its $10,000 adjusted basis. The $30,000 amount omits the $5,000 of services, which is taxed and therefore added to basis.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §722により、資産を出資して取得したパートナーシップ持分の取得価額は、出資した現金と出資資産の調整後取得価額の合計である。役務提供の対価として受け取った持分は課税される報酬であり（IRC §83、Treas. Reg. §1.721-1(b)(1)）、所得に算入した$5,000は持分の取得価額に加わる。

現金 = $20,000
資産（調整後取得価額）= $10,000
役務（所得算入額）= $5,000
持分の取得価額 = $35,000

$55,000は受け取った持分の時価、$50,000は資産を取得価額$10,000ではなく時価$30,000で計上した額である。$30,000は課税されて取得価額に加わる役務分$5,000を漏らしている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.18 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: Two partners each own an equal interest in a general partnership. One partner contributes to the partnership a building that has an adjusted basis of $40,000 and a fair market value of $60,000. The asset is subject to a mortgage of $30,000, which is assumed by the partnership. What is the contributing partner's share of liabilities in the partnership?
questions.explanation:
When a partnership assumes a liability of a contributing partner, the partner is treated as relieved of the entire liability (IRC §752(b)) and as taking on a share of the partnership's liabilities (§752(a)). In a general partnership with two equal partners, each partner bears the economic risk of loss for the mortgage equally (Treas. Reg. §1.752-2), so the contributing partner's share of the $30,000 liability is 50%.

Contributing partner's share = $30,000 × 50% = $15,000

The $30,000 amount is the full mortgage, which is the amount of liability relief, not the partner's continuing share. The $0 amount ignores that the partner still shares in partnership liabilities after the assumption, and the $40,000 amount is the building's adjusted basis, not a liability.
questions.explanationJa:
パートナーシップが出資パートナーの負債を引き受けると、そのパートナーは負債全額から解放されたものとされる（IRC §752(b)）一方、パートナーシップの負債の持分を引き受けたものとされる（§752(a)）。持分均等の2人のジェネラル・パートナーシップでは、両者が抵当債務の経済的損失リスクを均等に負うので（Treas. Reg. §1.752-2）、出資パートナーの持分は$30,000の50%である。

出資パートナーの負債の持分 = $30,000 × 50% = $15,000

$30,000は抵当債務全額で、解放された負債の額であり、引き続き負う持分ではない。$0は引受後もパートナーシップの負債を分担することを無視しており、$40,000は建物の取得価額で負債ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.38 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem:
A limited partnership agreement provides for the following profit allocation formula:

20% of the first $1,000,000 of profit, 25% of the next $1,000,000 of profit, and 30% of profit over $2,000,000 shall be allocated to the general partner.

Each limited partner and the general partner shall share equally in the remaining profit based on their relative percentages of ownership.

What profit amount should be allocated to a limited partner with 3% ownership if the total profit to be allocated is $4,500,000?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §704(a), a partner's distributive share of income is determined by the partnership agreement (subject to the substantial economic effect rules of §704(b)). The general partner first receives the tiered special allocation, and the remainder is shared by ownership percentage.

General partner special allocation:
20% × $1,000,000 = $200,000
25% × $1,000,000 = $250,000
30% × ($4,500,000 − $2,000,000) = $750,000
Total special allocation = $1,200,000
Remaining profit = $4,500,000 − $1,200,000 = $3,300,000
Share of a 3% limited partner = $3,300,000 × 3% = $99,000

The $135,000 amount applies 3% to the entire $4,500,000 and ignores the general partner's special allocation. The $101,250 amount applies a flat 25% to all profit ($4,500,000 × 75% × 3%). The $103,500 amount applies the 30% rate to only $2,000,000 instead of the full $2,500,000 over $2,000,000 ($4,500,000 − $1,050,000 = $3,450,000; × 3%).
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2018 Recently Released Q.15 (AICPA No. 64139)

questions.stem: Three equal partners formed partnership XYZ by each contributing $100,000 to the partnership. In the first year of operations, an $800,000 rental property was purchased in exchange for $200,000 in cash and a $600,000 recourse obligation. The partnership earned net income of $30,000 in its first year. What amount was each partner's basis in the partnership at the end of the first year?
questions.explanation:
A partner's outside basis equals contributions, plus the partner's share of partnership income (IRC §705(a)), plus the partner's share of partnership liabilities, which is treated as a contribution of money (§752(a)). Recourse liabilities are shared according to the partners' economic risk of loss (Treas. Reg. §1.752-2); with three equal partners each bears one-third of the $600,000 obligation. The $200,000 of cash paid for the property does not change basis, because it is the partnership's own cash.

Cash contribution = $100,000
Share of recourse liability = $600,000 / 3 = $200,000
Share of net income = $30,000 / 3 = $10,000
Ending basis = $310,000

The $100,000 amount reflects only the cash contribution. The $110,000 amount adds income but omits the share of the recourse liability. The $300,000 amount adds the liability share but omits the share of income.
questions.explanationJa:
パートナーの持分basisは、出資額に、パートナーシップの所得の持分（IRC §705(a)）と、現金出資とみなされるパートナーシップ負債の持分（§752(a)）を加えたものである。リコース負債は経済的損失リスクに応じて分担し（Treas. Reg. §1.752-2）、持分均等の3人なら$600,000の債務を各3分の1ずつ負う。不動産購入に使った現金$200,000はパートナーシップ自身の資金なのでbasisに影響しない。

現金出資 = $100,000
リコース負債の持分 = $600,000 ÷ 3 = $200,000
純利益の持分 = $30,000 ÷ 3 = $10,000
期末basis = $310,000

$100,000は現金出資だけ、$110,000は所得を加えたがリコース負債の持分を漏らした額、$300,000は負債の持分を加えたが所得の持分を漏らした額である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2018 Recently Released Q.16 (AICPA No. 64887)

questions.stem: Gavin, a 50% partner in the ABC Partnership, had a $4,000 basis at the beginning of the preceding year. During the preceding year, ABC incurred a $12,000 loss. In the current year, ABC reported $7,000 of ordinary income and made a $1,000 pro rata distribution. What is Gavin's basis at the end of the current year?
questions.explanation:
A partner's distributive share of partnership loss is allowed only to the extent of the partner's basis; the excess is suspended and carried forward (IRC §704(d)). In a later year, basis is first increased by income, then reduced by distributions, and only then reduced by losses, including suspended losses (Treas. Reg. §1.704-1(d)(2)).

Preceding year:
Share of loss = 50% x $12,000 = $6,000
Loss allowed = beginning basis $4,000; basis becomes $0
Suspended loss = $6,000 - $4,000 = $2,000

Current year:
Share of ordinary income = 50% x $7,000 = $3,500 -> basis $3,500
Share of pro rata distribution = 50% x $1,000 = $500 -> basis $3,000
Suspended loss now allowed = $2,000 -> basis $1,000

The $3,000 amount ignores the $2,000 suspended loss that becomes deductible once basis is restored. The $3,500 amount ignores both the distribution and the suspended loss. The $6,500 amount ignores the preceding year's loss entirely ($4,000 + $3,500 - $1,000).
questions.explanationJa:
パートナーが控除できる損失の配賦額は持分の取得価額（basis）が上限で、超過分は停止されて翌年以降に繰り越される（IRC §704(d)）。翌年以降は、まず所得で basis を増やし、次に分配で減らし、最後に損失（停止中の損失を含む）で減らす（Treas. Reg. §1.704-1(d)(2)）。

前年: 損失の配賦 50% × $12,000 = $6,000。控除できるのは basis $4,000 まで（basis は $0）、停止損失 $2,000。
当年: 所得の配賦 50% × $7,000 = $3,500 → basis $3,500
比例分配の配賦 50% × $1,000 = $500 → basis $3,000
停止損失 $2,000 を控除 → basis $1,000

$3,000 は basis 回復後に控除できる停止損失 $2,000 を無視している。$3,500 は分配と停止損失の両方を無視している。$6,500 は前年の損失をまったく反映していない（$4,000 + $3,500 − $1,000）。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2019 Recently Released Q.19 (AICPA No. 61803)

questions.stem: In year 1, a domestic LLC with two members elected classification as a corporation. In year 2, one of the members withdrew from the LLC. What is the LLC's tax classification for year 2 immediately after the member withdrew?

choices.label: B
choices.text: A liquidated corporation for tax purposes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A new entity eligible to make a classification election.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A single member LLC disregarded as separate from its owner.

questions.explanation:
Under the check-the-box regulations, an eligible entity's classification, once elected, continues until a new election is made. Treas. Reg. §301.7701-3(f)(2) provides that the classification of an eligible entity that has elected to be an association (taxed as a corporation) is not affected by a change in the number of its members. The LLC therefore remains classified as a corporation after one of its two members withdraws.

A member's withdrawal is not a liquidation of the corporation for tax purposes, and it does not create a new entity that makes a fresh classification election. The default disregarded-entity classification applies only to a single-member LLC that has not elected corporate classification; this LLC has an election in effect.
questions.explanationJa:
チェック・ザ・ボックス規則では、一度選択した分類は新たな選択をするまで継続する。Treas. Reg. §301.7701-3(f)(2) は、法人（association）として課税される選択をした事業体の分類は構成員数の変更の影響を受けないと定めている。したがって2人のうち1人が脱退しても、LLC は引き続き法人として扱われる。

構成員の脱退は税務上の法人の清算ではなく、新たな事業体が生じて分類選択をし直すこともない。無視される事業体（disregarded entity）となるのは法人課税を選択していない1人 LLC の原則的な分類であり、このLLCには法人課税の選択が有効に存在する。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2019 Recently Released Q.21 (AICPA No. 89182)

questions.stem:
Garner is a 25 percent partner in Classic General Partnership. On February 3, Garner's tax basis in Classic was $10,000 when she received a nonliquidating distribution of $5,000 cash. Classic had no unrealized receivables, appreciated inventory, or properties that had been contributed by its partners. Classic reported the following for the same year:

U.S. Treasury interest | $30,000
Ordinary business income | 120,000

What amount of income from Classic should Garner include in her gross income for that year?
questions.explanation:
A partner includes in gross income the partner's distributive share of partnership income for the year, whether or not distributed (IRC §702(a)). Interest on U.S. Treasury obligations is taxable for federal income tax purposes and is passed through as a separately stated item.

Share of Treasury interest = 25% x $30,000 = $7,500
Share of ordinary business income = 25% x $120,000 = $30,000
Total included = $37,500

The $5,000 cash distribution does not exceed Garner's $10,000 basis, so no gain is recognized on the distribution (IRC §731(a)); it only reduces basis.

The $7,500 amount includes only the Treasury interest, and the $30,000 amount includes only the ordinary business income. The $42,500 amount incorrectly adds the $5,000 distribution, which is a nontaxable return of basis.
questions.explanationJa:
パートナーは、分配の有無にかかわらず、その年のパートナーシップ所得の配賦額を総所得に含める（IRC §702(a)）。米国債の利息は連邦所得税の課税対象で、区分記載項目として配賦される。

米国債利息の配賦 = 25% × $30,000 = $7,500
事業所得の配賦 = 25% × $120,000 = $30,000
合計 = $37,500

現金分配 $5,000 は basis $10,000 を超えないので、分配による利得は認識されない（IRC §731(a)）。basis が減るだけである。

$7,500 は国債利息のみ、$30,000 は事業所得のみを含めている。$42,500 は非課税の basis の回収である分配 $5,000 を加えており誤り。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2019 Recently Released Q.33 (AICPA No. 57135)

questions.stem: Morse is a 50% partner in Ecco Partnership. Morse's tax basis in Ecco on January 2 was $4,000. Ecco did not have unrealized receivables, appreciated inventory, or properties that had been contributed by its partners. On December 31, Ecco made an $11,000 nonliquidating cash distribution to Morse. For the year, Ecco reported $10,000 of ordinary business income. What is the amount of the net capital gain realized by Morse from the cash distribution?
questions.explanation:
A partner recognizes gain on a nonliquidating distribution only to the extent cash distributed exceeds the partner's basis immediately before the distribution (IRC §731(a)(1)). Basis is first increased by the partner's distributive share of income for the year (IRC §705(a); Treas. Reg. §1.731-1(a)(1)(ii)), and the gain is capital gain because there are no unrealized receivables or appreciated inventory.

Beginning basis = $4,000
Share of ordinary income = 50% x $10,000 = $5,000
Basis before distribution = $9,000
Cash distributed = $11,000
Capital gain = $11,000 - $9,000 = $2,000

The $0 amount ignores that the cash exceeds basis. The $7,000 amount compares the cash with the beginning basis without adding the $5,000 share of income. The $11,000 amount treats the entire distribution as gain.
questions.explanationJa:
非清算分配では、分配された現金が分配直前の basis を超える部分についてのみ利得を認識する（IRC §731(a)(1)）。basis はまずその年の所得の配賦額で増やす（IRC §705(a)、Treas. Reg. §1.731-1(a)(1)(ii)）。未実現債権や値上がり棚卸資産がないので、利得はキャピタルゲインとなる。

期首 basis $4,000 + 所得の配賦 50% × $10,000 = $5,000 → 分配前 basis $9,000
現金分配 $11,000 − $9,000 = キャピタルゲイン $2,000

$0 は現金が basis を超えていることを無視している。$7,000 は所得の配賦 $5,000 を加えずに期首 basis と比べている。$11,000 は分配全額を利得としている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2019 Recently Released Q.39 (AICPA No. 56643)

questions.stem:
Vale is a 50% partner in Ball Partnership. Vale's tax basis in Ball on January 2, year 1, was $60,000. Ball did not have unrealized receivables, appreciated inventory, or properties that had been contributed by its partners. On December 31, year 1, Ball made a $10,000 nonliquidating cash distribution to each partner. The Ball Partnership income tax return reported the following items for year 1:

Tax-exempt interest income | $80,000
Dividend income | 12,000

What total amount of gross income from Ball should be included in Vale's year 1 adjusted gross income?
questions.explanation:
A partner includes in gross income only the distributive share of taxable partnership items (IRC §702(a)). Tax-exempt interest retains its character when passed through and is excluded from gross income (IRC §103(a)); it increases basis but is not included in AGI. The $10,000 cash distribution is less than Vale's basis, so it is a nontaxable reduction of basis (IRC §731(a)).

Share of dividend income = 50% x $12,000 = $6,000
Share of tax-exempt interest = 50% x $80,000 = $40,000 (excluded)
Gross income included = $6,000

The $16,000 amount adds the $10,000 distribution, which is not income. The $36,000 amount includes the $40,000 share of tax-exempt interest and the $6,000 dividend share and then subtracts the $10,000 distribution. The $46,000 amount includes the $40,000 share of tax-exempt interest.
questions.explanationJa:
パートナーが総所得に含めるのは、課税されるパートナーシップ項目の配賦額のみである（IRC §702(a)）。非課税利息は性質を保ったまま配賦され総所得から除外される（IRC §103(a)）。basis は増えるが AGI には含めない。現金分配 $10,000 は basis を下回るので、非課税で basis を減らすだけである（IRC §731(a)）。

配当の配賦 = 50% × $12,000 = $6,000
非課税利息の配賦 = 50% × $80,000 = $40,000（除外）
総所得に含める額 = $6,000

$16,000 は所得ではない分配 $10,000 を加えている。$36,000 は非課税利息の配賦 $40,000 と配当 $6,000 を含め、分配 $10,000 を差し引いている。$46,000 は非課税利息の配賦 $40,000 を含めている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part1 Q.15 (AICPA No. 56733)

questions.stem: Aston and Becker are equal partners in AB Partnership. In the tax year, the ordinary income of the partnership is $20,000, and the partnership has a long-term capital gain of $12,000. Aston's basis in AB was $40,000, and he received distributions of $5,000 during the year. What is Aston's share of AB's ordinary income?
questions.explanation:
Each partner takes into account the partner's distributive share of partnership ordinary income, determined under the partnership agreement (IRC §§702(a), 704(a)). Aston and Becker are equal partners, so Aston's share of ordinary income is 50% of $20,000. The long-term capital gain is a separately stated item, and distributions and basis do not change the distributive share.

Aston's share of ordinary income = 50% x $20,000 = $10,000

The $15,000 amount subtracts the $5,000 distribution from the $20,000 total. The $16,000 amount adds half of the $12,000 capital gain to the ordinary income share. The $18,500 amount is not derived from the distributive share rules.
questions.explanationJa:
各パートナーは、パートナーシップ契約に基づくパートナーシップの通常所得の配賦額を計上する（IRC §§702(a), 704(a)）。Aston と Becker は等分のパートナーなので、Aston の通常所得の配賦額は $20,000 の50%である。長期キャピタルゲインは区分記載項目であり、分配や basis は配賦額に影響しない。

Aston の通常所得の配賦額 = 50% × $20,000 = $10,000

$15,000 は $20,000 から分配 $5,000 を差し引いている。$16,000 は通常所得の配賦額にキャピタルゲイン $12,000 の半分を加えている。$18,500 は配賦の規定から導けない額である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part1 Q.16 (AICPA No. 58749)

questions.stem: Anne and Bart formed AB, LLC, a limited liability company, and elected to treat it as a partnership for tax purposes. Anne contributed $10,000 cash, and Bart contributed $5,000 cash, but Bart had a special skill that the partnership needed to be successful. The partnership agreement stated that Anne and Bart would both have a 50% interest in the LLC and that all profits and losses would be divided evenly between them. The LLC paid Bart $5,000 in year 1 for Bart's services to the partnership. The $5,000 would generally be reported to Bart as which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Payments to a partner for services that are determined without regard to the income of the partnership are guaranteed payments (IRC §707(c)). The partnership deducts them in computing ordinary business income, and the partner reports them as ordinary income (and, for a general partner or a partner providing services, as self-employment income). The $5,000 paid to Bart for his services is a guaranteed payment.

A partner is not an employee of the partnership, so the payment is not reported as salary or as wages on a Form W-2. Dividends are distributions of corporate earnings and profits; AB, LLC is taxed as a partnership, so it does not pay dividends.
questions.explanationJa:
パートナーが提供した役務の対価で、パートナーシップの所得に関係なく決まる支払は保証支払（guaranteed payment）である（IRC §707(c)）。パートナーシップは通常事業所得の計算上これを控除し、パートナーは通常所得として申告する。Bartへの役務対価$5,000は保証支払に当たる。

パートナーはパートナーシップの従業員ではないため、給与（salary）や賃金（wages）として報告されない。配当は法人のE&Pの分配であり、パートナーシップとして課税されるAB, LLCは配当を支払わない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.18 (AICPA No. 64877)

questions.stem: Hunter contributed artwork in exchange for a partnership interest. The artwork had an adjusted basis of $7,000, had a fair market value of $50,000, and was subject to a loan of $5,000. What is the partnership's basis in the artwork?
questions.explanation:
No gain or loss is recognized on a contribution of property in exchange for a partnership interest (IRC §721(a)), and the partnership takes a carryover basis in the contributed property equal to the contributing partner's adjusted basis, increased only by any gain recognized under §721(b) (IRC §723). The loan to which the artwork is subject affects Hunter's outside basis through the liability rules of IRC §752, but it does not change the partnership's basis in the artwork. The partnership's basis in the artwork is therefore $7,000.

The $50,000 amount uses the artwork's fair market value, but a §721 contribution is not a purchase. The $45,000 amount ($50,000 - $5,000) is the net fair market value of the contribution, which is relevant to Hunter's capital account, not to tax basis. The $2,000 amount ($7,000 - $5,000) subtracts the liability from the carryover basis; liability relief adjusts the contributing partner's basis in the partnership interest, not the partnership's basis in the property.
questions.explanationJa:
資産を拠出してパートナーシップ持分を取得しても損益は認識されず（IRC §721(a)）、パートナーシップは拠出したパートナーの調整後取得価額を引き継ぐ（§723。§721(b)により認識された利得があればその分だけ加算）。アートワークに付いている借入金は、§752の負債の規定を通じてHunterの持分の簿価（outside basis）に影響するが、パートナーシップ側のアートワークの簿価は変えない。したがってパートナーシップの簿価は$7,000。

$50,000は時価だが、§721の拠出は購入ではない。$45,000（$50,000 − $5,000）は拠出の正味時価で、資本勘定に関係する額であり税務簿価ではない。$2,000（$7,000 − $5,000）は引継価額から負債を差し引いているが、負債の移転で調整されるのは拠出したパートナーの持分の簿価であり、パートナーシップの資産の簿価ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.39 (AICPA No. 61939)

questions.stem: Coffee, Inc. and Tea, Inc., unrelated domestic corporations, decided to form a new partnership. Coffee has a December 31 year end and will own 75% of the new partnership. Tea has a June 30 year end and will own the remaining 25%. The new partnership wants to elect a fiscal tax year for business purposes. The new partnership may elect which of the following as its tax year end?
questions.explanation:
A partnership must generally use the tax year of its majority interest partners, meaning partners owning more than 50% of partnership profits and capital (IRC §706(b)(1)). Coffee owns 75% and uses a December 31 year end, so the partnership's required tax year ends December 31. A partnership may instead elect a different fiscal year under IRC §444, but only if the deferral period (the months between the end of the elected year and the end of the required year) is not more than three months (IRC §444(b)). The permissible fiscal year ends are therefore September 30, October 31, and November 30.

November 30 produces a one-month deferral and may be elected. February 28 would produce a ten-month deferral, June 30 a six-month deferral, and August 31 a four-month deferral, each of which exceeds the three-month limit. June 30 is Tea's year end, but Tea owns only 25% and is not a majority interest partner or a principal partner whose year controls.
questions.explanationJa:
パートナーシップは原則として、利益と資本の50%超を保有するパートナー（majority interest partners）の課税年度を使わなければならない（IRC §706(b)(1)）。Coffeeが75%を保有し12月31日決算なので、要求される課税年度は12月31日終了である。§444の選択により別の事業年度も選べるが、繰延期間（選択した年度の末日から要求される年度の末日までの月数）が3か月以内に限られる（§444(b)）。したがって選べるのは9月30日、10月31日、11月30日である。

11月30日は繰延期間が1か月なので選択できる。2月28日は10か月、6月30日は6か月、8月31日は4か月の繰延となり、いずれも3か月を超える。6月30日はTeaの決算日だが、Teaの持分は25%にすぎず、課税年度を決める立場にない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.40 (AICPA No. 101397)

questions.stem: A domestic limited liability company not classified as a corporation under IRS regulations is owned entirely by one individual taxpayer. Unless the taxpayer elects otherwise, the company will be taxed as
questions.explanation:
Under the check-the-box regulations, a domestic eligible entity with a single owner that does not elect to be classified as an association (corporation) is disregarded as an entity separate from its owner (Treas. Reg. §301.7701-3(b)(1)(ii)). A single-member LLC owned by an individual is therefore taxed as a disregarded entity, and its activity is reported on the owner's Form 1040 (for example, on Schedule C).

An LLC is never classified as a trust under these rules. Partnership classification is the default only for an eligible entity with two or more members. S corporation status requires the LLC first to elect to be classified as a corporation and then to make an S election; it is not the default.
questions.explanationJa:
チェック・ザ・ボックス規則では、所有者が1人の国内の適格事業体は、法人（association）として課税される選択をしない限り、所有者と別の事業体として扱われない（disregarded entity。Treas. Reg. §301.7701-3(b)(1)(ii)）。個人が単独で所有するLLCは、何も選択しなければ disregarded entity として課税され、その活動は所有者のForm 1040（Schedule C等）で申告する。

LLCがこの規則で信託として分類されることはない。パートナーシップ課税がデフォルトになるのは構成員が2人以上の場合だけである。S法人として課税されるには法人課税の選択とSの選択が必要で、デフォルトではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.41 (AICPA No. 68769)

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the taxation of a partner in a partnership?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Partners must include their share of partnership capital gains as ordinary income on their personal income tax returns.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a partner's loss is limited in one tax year because of the at-risk rules, it may be carried forward to a later year, subject to that year's at-risk computation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Passive activity losses may be used to offset both passive activity income and portfolio income.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A partner's loss is limited to the fair market value of their partnership interest.

questions.explanation:
A loss disallowed under the at-risk rules is treated as a deduction allocable to the same activity in the next tax year (IRC §465(a)(2)). It is carried forward and may be deducted in a later year to the extent the partner's at-risk amount in that year permits.

The character of partnership items is determined at the partnership level and flows through to the partners (IRC §702(b)), so a partner's share of capital gains remains capital gain, not ordinary income. Passive activity losses may offset only passive activity income, not portfolio income (IRC §469). A partner's deductible loss is limited by the partner's adjusted basis in the partnership interest (IRC §704(d)), not by the interest's fair market value.
questions.explanationJa:
at-risk規則で否認された損失は、翌年度の同じ活動に配分される控除として扱われる（IRC §465(a)(2)）。つまり繰り越され、その年のat-risk額の範囲で後の年度に控除できる。

パートナーシップの項目の性質はパートナーシップ段階で決まり、そのままパートナーに引き継がれる（§702(b)）ので、キャピタルゲインの配分額は通常所得ではなくキャピタルゲインのままである。パッシブ活動損失はパッシブ所得とだけ相殺でき、ポートフォリオ所得とは相殺できない（§469）。損失控除の上限は持分の時価ではなく、持分の税務簿価である（§704(d)）。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2021 Recently Released Q.13 (AICPA No. 64299)

questions.stem:
Two partners each have a 50% interest in the partnership's capital and profits. The December 31, year 3, balance sheet for the partnership is listed below.

Adjusted Basis | Fair Market Value
Cash | $ 25,000 | $ 25,000
Land | 75,000 | 375,000
Total Assets | $100,000 | $400,000

Adjusted Basis | Fair Market Value
Capital A | $ 50,000 | $200,000
Capital D | 50,000 | 200,000
Total Capital | $100,000 | $400,000

On January 1, year 4, one partner purchased half of the other partner's interest in the partnership for $100,000. A valid Section 754 election is in place. What is the adjusted tax basis of the partnership's assets after this transaction?
questions.explanation:
When a partnership interest is sold and a §754 election is in effect, the partnership adjusts the basis of its property with respect to the purchasing partner by the difference between the purchaser's basis in the acquired interest and the purchaser's share of the partnership's adjusted basis in its property (IRC §743(b)). The adjustment is allocated among the partnership's assets under IRC §755 (here, to the appreciated land).

Interest purchased: half of a 50% interest = 25%.
Purchaser's outside basis in the acquired interest: $100,000.
Purchaser's share of inside basis: $100,000 × 25% = $25,000.
Section 743(b) adjustment: $100,000 - $25,000 = $75,000.
Adjusted basis of partnership assets: $100,000 + $75,000 = $175,000.

The $100,000 amount is the basis of partnership assets with no adjustment, which would be correct only without a §754 election. The $200,000 amount adds the full $100,000 purchase price to the existing basis instead of only the excess over the purchaser's share of inside basis. The $400,000 amount is the fair market value of the partnership's assets; only the purchased 25% interest is adjusted, not all assets.
questions.explanationJa:
§754の選択がある場合にパートナーシップ持分が売買されると、パートナーシップは、購入者の持分の簿価と、購入者に帰属するパートナーシップ資産の調整後簿価との差額だけ、購入者に関する資産の簿価を調整する（IRC §743(b)）。調整額は§755により資産に配分される（本問では含み益のある土地）。

購入した持分: 50%の半分 = 25%
購入者の持分の簿価（outside basis）: $100,000
購入者に帰属する資産簿価（inside basis）: $100,000 × 25% = $25,000
§743(b)調整額: $100,000 − $25,000 = $75,000
調整後のパートナーシップ資産の簿価: $100,000 + $75,000 = $175,000

$100,000は調整前の資産簿価で、§754の選択がない場合の金額である。$200,000は、購入者の持分相当の簿価を超える部分ではなく、購入代金$100,000全額を既存の簿価に加えている。$400,000は資産の時価であり、調整されるのは購入した25%持分に関する部分だけである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2021 Recently Released Q.37 (AICPA No. 100669)
